chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amer, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Hisham ibn Salim. He said: al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) said:
It is unjust for a rider to say to one who is walking: 'The road!' (i.e., get out of my way).

key_terms.الجور: Jawr - injustice, tyranny, oppression; deviation from the right path
key_terms.الراكب: The rider - one mounted on an animal or conveyance
key_terms.الطريق: The road/way - used here as an imperious demand meaning "clear the road"
key_terms.الماشي: The walker/pedestrian - one traveling on foot

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about a rider telling a pedestrian to move out of the way?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that it is a form of injustice (jawr) for a person riding an animal to demand that a pedestrian clear the road for them. This hadith, narrated in a public assembly in Rabi' al-Awwal 368 AH, reflects the Imam's emphasis on social courtesy and the rights of the vulnerable, condemning the arrogance of those in positions of advantage over others sharing public spaces.
word_analysis: the road (get out of the way)

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. Muhammad .b Masrur (ra) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. `Amer narrated to us from his uncle `Abdullah b. `Amer from Muhammad b. Isma`il b. Bazi` from Hisham b. Salim. He said: Al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as) said:
It is unjust for a rider to say to one who is walking: “The road (i.e. get out of my way).”
